summary: Agree it is PARTIAL. Parts 1 to 3 shipped in #710 and follow-ups: the raw-frame decode mark, the sidebar commit and painted marks with their measures, a deterministic fixture generator with 30 projects and 2,000 threads, harness collection of ryco:startup:* measures, a 100 us CDP boot CPU profile summarized per source file, and gates on longTaskTotalMs and shellPaintedMs. I checked the frame probe against the real wire format: effect 4.0.2 RpcServer sends a JSON text frame shaped {"_tag":"Chunk","requestId":...}, so the regex matches on the direct /ws path. Part 4 is only partly done: no shell upserts and no actualDuration budgets. Part 5 has no web micro-benchmarks, and the sidebar-commit-count gate is missing. I also found two small defects the auditor missed: perf:compare cannot produce source-level CPU summaries, and the decode measure is recorded again with a wrong value after reconnects.

evidence.note: createPrimaryShellFrameProbe marks primary-shell-frame-received on the first raw text frame that matches "_tag":"Chunk","requestId":<shell id>. Its listener is registered at socket construction, before Effect's own listener, so it runs before JSON parse and Schema decode.

The probe is wired only on the direct primary WsTransport (onRequestStart + webSocketConstructor). The hosted relay transport above (~:930-960) has no probe, so hosted boot records no decode measure. That is out of scope, not a defect.

responseEnvelope builds {_tag:'Chunk',requestId,values} and the socket server writes JSON.stringify output as a text frame. apps/server/src/ws.ts:79 uses RpcServer.toHttpEffectWebsocket with RpcSerialization.layerJson, so the probe's string/regex assumption holds for direct and desktop boot.
onShellSnapshotReceived marks snapshot-received and measures primary-shell-decode (frame-received to snapshot-received) on every primary shell snapshot, including reconnects.

A layout effect on the first live bootstrapComplete marks primary-sidebar-committed, then markStartupPhaseAfterPaint (rAF, then a MessageChannel task). Cache hydration leaves bootstrapComplete false (persistence/primaryShellCache.ts:20-25), so the mark is live-only. It is mounted at AppSidebarLayout.tsx:316, in the same commit as the statically imported ThreadSidebar (:7, :308).
STARTUP_MEASURES adds primary-sidebar-commit, primary-shell-paint, primary-shell-painted (from navigation start) and primary-cached-sidebar-committed.

The harness reads every ryco:startup:* measure (collectStartupMeasures :183) and waits up to 10 s for the painted measure. Its CPU profile runs Profiler.start before goto and Profiler.stop at painted + 5 s, with summarizeCpuProfile and createDistSourceResolver.

Defect: compare-refs always builds with env RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP: '0'. command.ts:24 merges this over process.env, so it overrides the user's setting. perf:compare --cpu-profile therefore never gets .map files, and its summaries fall back to content-hashed chunk names (cpuProfile.ts:154-155, scriptLabel), which do not match across refs. This contradicts docs/performance-testing.md:159-161. The '0' looks deliberate, because measureWebBundle (bundleMeasurement.ts:19-31) counts every dist file, .map files included.

DEFAULT_COMPARISON_POLICY gates longTaskTotalMs and shellPaintedMs. No sidebar commit/render-count metric exists. Other startupMeasures (decode, sidebar-commit) are stored per sample but not compared or shown in report.ts.

The fixture generator drives the real orchestration engine, with 30 projects, 2,000 threads, 60% archived, 0 to 5 worktrees per project with feature/* branches, and threads attached to worktrees. It omits drafts on purpose because they are client-side. Run via perf:fixture-home; cli.ts:71-72 documents it.

The test mounts Sidebar in React.Profiler with 30 projects and 2,000 threads, applies 30 streaming thread-detail events and model-picker toggles, and asserts 0 extra commits and renders. It applies no shell upserts (no applyShellEvents), checks no actualDuration (onRender ignores its arguments), sets no absolute mount commit ceiling, and covers projects mode only, not the inbox / buildInboxSidebarModel.

The only web/client micro-benchmark (approximateJsonSize). git ls-files contains no .perf-research or bench files for shell decode, syncServerShellSnapshot, the sidebar chain, composeSidebarTree or buildInboxSidebarModel. Only output/perf-research-2026-10-11/ryco-performance-report.html is committed.
usePerfMark still registers a deps-less useLayoutEffect per render when disabled. This is unchanged and negligible.

remaining: (1) Part 5 is not done. There are no committed micro-benchmarks for web boot pure functions (shell frame JSON parse plus Schema decode, useStore.syncServerShellSnapshot in apps/web/src/store.ts, the sidebar derivation chain in apps/web/src/components/sidebar/hooks/useSidebarTree.ts and sidebarProjectTreeCache.ts, composeSidebarTree, and buildInboxSidebarModel in apps/web/src/components/inboxSidebar/inboxSidebarModel.ts). scripts/perf/micro holds only client-retained-size.ts. (2) Part 4 is partial. Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx:166-187 applies 30 thread-detail events but no shell upserts, has no actualDuration budget, sets no initial-mount commit ceiling, and does not cover inbox mode. (3) Part 3's 'gate on sidebar commit count' is missing. No metric in scripts/perf/model.ts PerfMetricKey or DEFAULT_COMPARISON_POLICY, and the harness collects no sidebar render count during boot. (4) The startupMeasures beyond shellPaintedMs, such as primary-shell-decode and primary-sidebar-commit, appear only in the raw per-sample JSON. They are neither compared nor shown in the Markdown report.
fixDefects: (a) scripts/perf/gitComparison.ts:60 always builds compared refs with RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP=0, overriding the environment. perf:compare --cpu-profile can never produce the per-source summary that docs/performance-testing.md:159-161 and the cpuProfile.ts header describe. It falls back to content-hashed chunk names that differ between base and candidate, which makes cross-ref profile comparison awkward. The override looks intentional, because bundleMeasurement.ts counts .map files. (b) apps/web/src/environments/runtime/service.ts:197-205 calls measureStartupPhase('primary-shell-decode', 'primary-shell-frame-received', 'primary-shell-snapshot-received') on every primary shell snapshot. The probe stands down after the first mark, and performance.measure uses the latest mark of each name. After any reconnect, a new primary-shell-decode measure therefore spans from the first boot's frame to the reconnect snapshot, a bogus value of minutes or hours. The pre-existing primary-shell-snapshot and primary-shell-ready measures have the same pattern. The harness is unaffected because it reads measures once, before its reconnect phase. Anyone reading ryco:startup:* after a reconnect, or taking the latest entry, gets a wrong decode time. Both defects are low severity.
implementationSketch: Defects first (S). (a) In scripts/perf/gitComparison.ts measureRef, build with RYCO_WEB_SOURCEMAP: input.scenario.cpuProfileDir ? 'hidden' : '0'. Make measureWebBundle skip *.map in scripts/perf/bundleMeasurement.ts filesBelow, so bundle metrics stay comparable either way, and add a test in bundleMeasurement.test.ts. If maps stay off instead, correct the docs wording. (b) In service.ts onShellSnapshotReceived, record primary-shell-decode only on the first primary snapshot: capture `const first = !hasReachedStartupPhase('primary-shell-snapshot-received')` before markStartupPhase and only measure when it is true. Optionally guard the snapshot and ready measures the same way. Add a unit test next to startupInstrumentation.test.ts or service tests asserting that one decode measure exists after two snapshots. Remaining work (M). (1) Micro-benchmarks: extract makeSnapshot from Sidebar.renders.browser.tsx into a shared deterministic fixture, e.g. apps/web/src/test/fixtures/largeShellSnapshot.ts (30 projects, 2,000 threads, 60% archived, some worktrees). Add scripts/perf/micro/web-shell-boot.ts, runnable with Node like client-retained-size.ts. It should time: JSON.parse of a Chunk frame plus Schema decode of the subscribeShell item schema from @ryco/contracts; useStore.getState().syncServerShellSnapshot (check that apps/web/src/store.ts imports cleanly under Node, otherwise use vitest bench via vite-plus in apps/web); the useSidebarTree pure helpers and composeSidebarTree; and buildInboxSidebarModel. Use warmup plus N iterations and print median and p95 in µs. Reference the script from docs/performance-testing.md. (2) Sidebar render test: after the streaming loop, apply 50 shell upserts for an unrelated thread through useStore.getState().applyShellEvents (environmentStateSink.ts:48 is the runtime path), using a thread.meta-updated or thread.created-style shell event. Assert a bounded Sidebar commit count, e.g. <= 50, or equal to the number of rows that actually change. Capture actualDuration in onRender and assert a generous ceiling on the max per commit (or log only, to avoid CI flakiness). Add an absolute ceiling on initial-mount commits. Add a second case with setSidebarMode('inbox'). (3) Boot sidebar commit gate: React.Profiler onRender does not fire in production builds, so count renders with a cheap module counter in Sidebar (usePerfMark already runs per render). At primary-shell-painted, publish the count as a measure or mark detail, e.g. performance.mark('ryco:startup:sidebar-renders', {detail: n}). Read it in browserProbe readBrowserVitals, add sidebarBootRenders to PerfMetricKey and DEFAULT_COMPARISON_POLICY with an absolute floor such as 2, and add a model/comparison test. (4) Add the startupMeasures and cpuProfile top entries to scripts/perf/report.ts output.
decisionReason: Test and measurement tooling only. It touches no auth, E2EE, hosted lifecycle or Hub protocol, and causes no product behaviour change.
